page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Edsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor is equipped with 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics and tradeoffs for this hardware configuration. The single-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2215.58. However, due to the low core count of a single physical core, multi-core CPU performance is poor, scoring 2263.98 in stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score is average at 1927.71, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths are poor at 22.92 GB/sec and 12.15 GB/sec respectively. Small-block cached read bandwidth is measured at 168.1 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are weak, with Redis achieving 4.01 million operations per second. For lightweight AI workloads, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 88.94 tokens per second on a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing speeds remain weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2ds_v7 offers a specialized resource profile that avoids the expense of high vCPU counts while maintaining a generous 16.0 GB memory allocation and fast local NVMe storage. This makes it a qualitatively efficient choice for workloads that are memory-bound rather than compute-bound. Appropriate workloads include small-scale databases, caching layers, lightweight web serving (with static throughput measured at 4.95 GB/sec), and basic analytical tasks that fit within the memory envelope without requiring heavy multi-threaded processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core, 2 threads), 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions. Benchmarks indicate average single-core CPU and PassMark memory performance, though multi-core compute and uncached memory bandwidth are limited by the dual-vCPU configuration. This instance provides a qualitatively cost-effective profile for memory-intensive, low-scale workloads. It is best suited for small databases, caching layers, and lightweight web serving.
